title: Supply and Demand
text: Supply and demand is the fundamental economic model describing how prices are determined in a market economy. The law of demand states that, all else being equal, as the price of a good rises, the quantity demanded falls. The law of supply states that as the price rises, the quantity supplied increases. The point where supply and demand curves intersect is the equilibrium price, at which the quantity demanded equals the quantity supplied. Changes in factors other than price — income, consumer preferences, input costs, technology — shift the supply or demand curves, causing prices to adjust to a new equilibrium. This model was first formalized by Alfred Marshall in his 1890 work Principles of Economics.
